rows.label: Battle of Harlem Heights
rows.quote: Greene saw combat for the first time in the Battle of Harlem Heights

rows.label: Battle of Fort Washington
rows.quote: where Washington, Greene, Putnam and Hugh Mercer were located
rows.note: Greene then crossed to Fort Lee.

rows.label: Fort Lee (evacuated)
rows.quote: Washington and Greene quickly ordered the evacuation of the fort

rows.label: Battle of Trenton
rows.quote: infantry divisions commanded by Major Generals Nathanael Greene and John Sullivan

rows.label: Battle of Princeton
rows.quote: Major Generals Henry Knox and Nathanael Greene talked him out of it
rows.note: Presence at Princeton also stated in Greene article (commanded part of the army).

rows.label: Battle of Brandywine
rows.quote: Washington and Greene arrived with reinforcements to try to hold off the British

rows.label: Battle of Germantown
rows.quote: Nathanael Greene's column on Limekiln Road had finally caught up

rows.label: Valley Forge (winter quarters)
rows.quote: Greene joined with the rest of Washington's army in establishing a camp at Valley Forge
rows.note: Date is the encampment start date (Valley Forge article: from December 19, 1777); Greene article says only 'In December'. Less certain.

rows.label: Battle of Monmouth
rows.quote: he ordered Greene to take Brigadier General William Woodford's brigade

rows.label: Battle of Rhode Island
rows.quote: General Greene concentrated his forces in front of Turkey Hill

rows.label: Springfield, NJ (blocks Knyphausen)
rows.quote: Major General Nathanael Greene had 1,500 Continental troops and 500 New Jersey Militia

rows.label: Charlotte (takes Southern command)
rows.quote: took formal command of the Southern Theater
rows.note: Cowpens article also has Morgan reporting to Greene's HQ at Charlotte on Dec 3.

rows.label: Trading Ford / Salisbury (joins Morgan)
rows.quote: Greene joined Daniel Morgan's Continentals at Trading Ford on the Yadkin River
rows.note: Trading Ford has no Wikipedia coordinates; Salisbury is the nearby town. Another source says Greene evacuated Salisbury stores Feb 2.

rows.label: Guilford Court House (rendezvous)
rows.quote: Greene reached Guilford Courthouse on February 7.

rows.label: Crosses the Dan River
rows.quote: Greene's force outpaced the British and crossed the Dan River on February 14
rows.note: Crossed at Irwin's/Boyd's Ferries near South Boston. Some accounts give Feb 13 for Greene himself and Feb 14 for Williams' rear guard. Corrected after independent check: Greene himself crossed the Dan on Feb 13; his rear guard crossed on the 14th (Emerging Revolutionary War).

rows.label: Recrosses the Dan
rows.quote: On 22 February Greene moved his army south across the Dan
rows.note: Same ferry area as the first crossing.

rows.label: Alamance Creek camp
rows.quote: Greene camped on the north side of the creek
rows.note: Approximate location of Alamance Creek camp.

rows.label: Battle of Guilford Court House
rows.quote: Major General Nathanael Greene's 4,500 Americans

rows.label: Camden (Hobkirk's Hill camp)
rows.quote: Greene chose to encamp his army about a mile and a half away

rows.label: Battle of Hobkirk's Hill
rows.quote: 1,550 American regulars and militia under Major General Nathanael Greene

rows.label: Siege of Ninety Six begins
rows.quote: Greene and about 1,000 men arrived outside Ninety Six on May 22

rows.label: Assault on Star Fort fails
rows.quote: Greene launched an unsuccessful attack on the British fort at Ninety Six
rows.note: Date of assault stated in Siege of Ninety Six article (June 18).

rows.label: High Hills of Santee (rest camp)
rows.quote: On 16 July, Greene moved his army

rows.label: Fort Motte
rows.quote: By 4 Sept., they were camped at Fort Motte

rows.label: Battle of Eutaw Springs
rows.quote: Greene's army began marching from Burdell's Plantation

rows.label: Charleston (British evacuate)
rows.quote: At 3 o'clock, p.m. General Greene conducted Governor Mathews
rows.note: Moultrie memoir quoted by CCPL; some accounts say Wayne's 400 men entered first around 11 a.m.
